people.name: Prannoy Roy
people.role: Psephologist and journalist, a founder of NDTV, who now presents DeKoder.
people.intro: In a seven-minute episode on 8 October 2026 he sets the names West Bengal left off or deleted beside the swing against the TMC, and sets the women and the Muslim electors among them beside their shares of the roll.

pieces.title: More SIR Deletions, Bigger BJP Swing? Prannoy Roy DeKodes the Data | DeKoder

claims.quote: In the 25 constituencies with the highest SIR deletion rates, the TMC had a swing against it of nearly 10.5% ... in the 25 constituency with the lowest SIR deletions, the swing against the TMC was down to only 5.3% ... [SIR] deletions almost doubled the swing against the TMC.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: He does not name the data behind the two swing figures. The comparison sets the 25 seats that lost the most names against the 25 that lost the fewest, with nothing to allow for other ways those seats differ, and the episode does not define the rate it calls the deletion rate.
claims.site: West Bengal's own figures show why other differences matter. Measured by the fall in the roll, the most affected districts are Kolkata North at 27.98 per 100 and Kolkata South at 24.54, and the least affected is Purbo Medinipur at 1.64. By seat the range runs from 39.74 in Chowrangee to 0.34 in Patashpur, so the seats at either end sit in different parts of the state with different histories of voting. In Bihar, the one state where the site has fitted a model of the swing, leaving out each seat's lead at the previous election turns a slope of +0.31 into -0.83.
claims.stops: The site has not fitted a swing model for West Bengal. A vote count also cannot show whether the names left off or deleted moved votes from one party to another.

claims.quote: women deletions accounted for 62% of all deleted names compared with only 38% of men voters deleted.
claims.rests: The figure matches the Sabar Institute's count as BehanBox reported it, 61.8 per cent. That count takes names left off or deleted and names held for adjudication together.
claims.site: The Chief Electoral Officer's own counts give smaller shares. Women were 53.5 per cent of the 58.2 lakh names left off the draft, against 49.2 per cent of the roll, and 52.6 per cent of the fall from the 2024 roll to the roll at the 2026 nominations. They were over-represented in 21 of 24 districts.
claims.stops: The Chief Electoral Officer has published no split by sex of the adjudication outcomes, so the site cannot check the larger figure.

claims.quote: In other words, the SIR deletion process clearly targeted Muslim voters ... Muslim voter deletions were at a 52% higher deletion rate than non-Muslims.
claims.rests: He does not say how the religion of the electors left off or deleted was found. It can only be guessed from names, as the Sabar Institute did. His rate comparison is consistent with his own figures, 30 lakh against 19.8 lakh. The word targeted is a claim about purpose drawn from a pattern.
claims.site: The site does not classify the names West Bengal left off or deleted by religion. In Bihar, where it does, the religion of those left off is guessed from names and given as a range, because some names cannot be classified. The census share falls inside that range in 18 of 38 districts and below it in 20.
claims.stops: Names give only a guess at religion, and the lists record no purpose. The site makes no claim about what anyone intended.

claims.quote: there's no doubt and there never has been any doubt that election [rolls] need to be constantly updated and cleaned up

strongest: The shares left off the draft that he gives for Delhi, Maharashtra and Karnataka, about 33, 21 and 20 per cent, are right as reported.
He asks the Commission to explain the gaps by sex and by religion, and the site lacks that data too.
further: Saying the names left off or deleted almost doubled the swing reads a cause into a raw comparison of two groups of seats.
Saying the process clearly targeted Muslim voters asserts a purpose that the figures cannot show.
He says the millions left off will now be unable to vote, which leaves out the names put back through Form 6 and appeals.

people.name: The Indian Express
people.role: National daily. The investigation is by Ritika Chopra, its Resident Editor in Mumbai, and the paper later released its special issue free.
people.intro: On 23 September 2026 the paper reported that two Election Commissioners had objected on record to steps taken in the Commission's name. The account rests on documents the paper holds, and it keeps the failures of process apart from the election result.

pieces.title: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
'Differing views' part of 'decision-making', says EC, does not address concerns two ECs red-flagged

claims.quote: Sandhu and Joshi have formally objected, on record, at least 14 times over the last 10 months – four times on a single day – to decisions taken and orders issued, they say, without their knowledge.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: Documents the paper holds and the site has not seen. The Commission's reply spoke of written notes and differing views and did not deny that the notes exist.
claims.site: The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists each dated objection with the special issue's page number, and gives the paper's count of 14 in its text.
claims.stops: The site has seen only the paper's account of the notes.

claims.quote: On May 16, Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded on file that the form 'cannot be altered without making amendments in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960' ... Sandhu concurred on May 19. In July, the SIR declaration appeared on the online form anyway.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: The Form 6 declaration itself can be seen on the online form, and the paper reported it on 12 July 2026. The file notes are the paper's.
claims.site: The section on Form 6 on the process page sets out the declaration and the objections to it.
claims.stops: No count exists of the applications the declaration held up.

claims.quote: Of the 294 seats that went to polls, in 49, the SIR deletions exceeded the victory margin. But in these, the spoils were almost evenly shared — 26 were won by BJP and 21 by TMC.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: The paper does not say which count of names it used. Its figures match Newslaundry's third test, which used the names held for adjudication from the Sabar Institute's data. In the line before, the paper says there was no evidence of the revision's role in the outcome.
claims.site: The Chief Electoral Officer published no count of names left off below the state, so the site measures the fall in the roll from 2024 instead. On that measure the fall exceeds the 2026 margin in 139 of 294 seats. Seats the AITC won lost 12.38 per 100 and seats the BJP won lost 9.41, and set against their own districts the gap shrinks to 0.23 against 0.03.
claims.stops: A fall larger than the margin shows that it could have decided the seat. It cannot show that it did.

claims.quote: the manner in which names were struck off prompted the Supreme Court, in February 2026, to take the last leg of the SIR out of the Commission's hands and get judicial officers to decide on the plight of 60 lakh voters flagged for "logical discrepancies." Of these, 27 lakh electors were subsequently deleted by the Commission.
claims.rests: The totals match the official figures as reported.
claims.site: In West Bengal 60,06,675 names were held for adjudication and 27,16,393 were found not eligible. Of the appeals, 16,10,311, or 49.3 per cent, were against a name's inclusion.
claims.stops: Who filed the 16 lakh appeals against inclusion is not public. The paper says the Commission did not say.

claims.quote: Goa's EROs heard these cases. On the documents produced, they found 97 voters eligible for the final roll. The software had no way to record that decision.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: Documents as the paper reports them.
claims.site: The process page carries the Goa sequence from the special issue, marked as press. Goa left 1,00,042 names off its draft, 8.44 for every 100 electors.
claims.stops: The 97 are the paper's count, and the site holds no list of them.

strongest: It rests on dated documents. It put questions to the Commission and printed the Commission's later press note in full.
It keeps the failures of process apart from the election result in so many words.
further: Very little. Its description of the disquiet as unprecedented in scale and significance is a judgement, and the paper presents it as its own.

people.name: Ravish Kumar
people.role: Journalist and broadcaster, formerly of NDTV India, who publishes daily commentary in Hindi on his own YouTube channel.
people.intro: His episodes of 23 September and 1 October 2026 follow the Express investigation closely. The translations from Hindi are the site's. Where he relays a party leader's figures, the panel says whose they are.

pieces.title: खुल गई पोल, सामने आ गया खेल, एक्सप्रेस की रिपोर्ट से मचा तहलका
pieces.title_en: The truth is out, the game exposed: the Express report causes an uproar

pieces.title: मुस्लिम वोटर का नाम कौन कटवा रहा है, FORM-7 के पीछे गिरोह?  FORM-6 पर राहुल के सवाल पर EC चुप क्यों?
pieces.title_en: Who is getting Muslim voters' names struck off, a gang behind Form 7? Why is the EC silent on Rahul's question about Form 6?

claims.quote: 10 महीने में 14 बार दो-दो चुनाव आयुक्तों ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त से असहमति जाहिर की है।
claims.translation: In 10 months, two Election Commissioners have expressed disagreement with the Chief Election Commissioner 14 times.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: The count of 14 matches the Express. The paper describes them as objections to decisions taken and orders issued without the two Commissioners' knowledge, which is narrower than disagreement with the Chief Election Commissioner.
claims.site: The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists each dated objection with the special issue's page number, and gives the paper's count of 14 in its text.
claims.stops: The site has seen only the paper's account of the notes.

claims.quote: वोट चोरी का सिस्टम पकड़ा गया है। यह सिस्टम कहीं और नहीं चुनाव आयोग के भीतर पकड़ा गया है।
claims.translation: The system of vote theft has been caught. It has been caught nowhere else but inside the Election Commission.
claims.rests: The Express reports objections about process, about access to the roll software, Form 6 and appeals. It reports no theft of votes, and on West Bengal it says there was no evidence of the revision's role in the outcome.
claims.site: Nothing on the site measures purpose.
claims.stops: The lists cannot show what anyone intended, and the site does not say whether anything was stolen.

claims.quote: 97 लोगों ने साबित कर दिया कि वोटर लिस्ट में उनका नाम होना चाहिए ... जिस अधिकारी के सामने दावा किया वो मान भी गया लेकिन दिल्ली से कंट्रोल हो रहा सॉफ्टवेयर उनका नाम वोटर लिस्ट में नहीं जोड़ता है।
claims.translation: 97 people proved they should be on the roll ... the officer accepted their claim, but the software controlled from Delhi did not add them.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: This matches the Express account of Goa.
claims.site: The process page carries the Goa sequence from the special issue, marked as press. Goa left 1,00,042 names off its draft, 8.44 for every 100 electors.
claims.stops: The 97 are the paper's count, and the site holds no list of them.

claims.quote: मीडिया ने भी 13 करोड़ लोगों का चेहरा गायब कर दिया।
claims.translation: The media too made the faces of 13 crore people disappear.
claims.rests: He names no source in this line. The figure matches the Express, which reports more than 13 crore names left off the draft rolls.
claims.site: The site's own sum across the 31 states and union territories with a draft is 13,39,03,307 names left off. In the states that published a full split by reason, about a fifth were entered as dead. In several states the final roll is larger than the draft.
claims.stops: The 13 crore are names left off draft rolls before anything was put back, and they include the dead and the duplicates. The site cannot say how many of them were eligible electors.

claims.quote: पश्चिम बंगाल में 27 लाख वोटरों को चुनाव में वोट देने का मौका नहीं मिला।
claims.translation: In West Bengal, 27 lakh voters did not get the chance to vote in the election.
claims.rests: This matches the state totals as reported. Of the 60,06,675 names held for adjudication, 27,16,393 were found not eligible.
claims.site: The West Bengal page also gives 32,68,119 found eligible and 37,05,235 appeals pending, as reported. Only 1,607 names were restored before the poll.
claims.stops: These are state totals as reported. With most appeals still pending, the site cannot say how many of the 27 lakh were eligible.

claims.quote: 20 अगस्त से 24 सितंबर के बीच 29,000 से ज्यादा फॉर्म सेवन भरे गए हैं। इनमें से 93% आम लोगों ने भरे हैं।
claims.translation: Between 20 August and 24 September more than 29,000 Form 7s were filed [in Karnataka], 93% of them by ordinary people.
claims.rests: He gives these as the figures of Rizwan Arshad, a Karnataka minister, from the minister's letter to the Chief Electoral Officer.
claims.site: The Disputes page lists the bulk Form 7 objections reported in Karnataka, each with its source. Karnataka's own pages carry the Chief Electoral Officer's district figures only.
claims.stops: The Chief Electoral Officer has published no count of Form 7s by who filed them, so the 93 per cent cannot be set against an official figure.

claims.quote: नए वोटर और बहुत से पुराने वोटर के लिए इसका प्रमाण देना मुश्किल होने लगा और उनका नाम वोटर लिस्ट से कटने लगा।
claims.translation: For new voters and many old ones, proving this became difficult and their names began to be struck off the roll.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on the rolls
claims.rests: Form 6 is the application for new enrolment. The declaration could delay or block an application, and the Express says applicants could not submit without answering it. No source found shows it deleting names already on the roll.
claims.site: The section on Form 6 on the process page sets out the declaration and the Commissioners' objections.
claims.stops: No count exists of Form 6 applications refused because of the declaration.

strongest: He follows the Express documents closely, and the figures he relays from them are right as reported.
The West Bengal adjudication figure he uses, 27 lakh, is the reported official one.
He relays a Bombay High Court bench's remarks on Goa, which are about process and can be checked.
further: He moves from the paper's findings about process to vote theft, which the paper itself does not claim.
He treats the 13 crore names left off the drafts as people erased.

people.name: Yogendra Yadav
people.role: Psephologist and political activist. He is one of the petitioners in the Supreme Court challenge to the Bihar revision and made submissions in person. He was with Lokniti at CSDS, is the founding national president of Swaraj India, a registered party, and convenes Bharat Jodo Abhiyan.
people.intro: His main method sets the roll against the projected adult population, which catches the young adults a count of names left off cannot see. The quotations are from reports of his submissions in court and of his talks.

pieces.title: 'Bihar SIR Is Intensive Deletion Exercise' : Yogendra Yadav Appears In Supreme Court With Two Persons Deleted As Dead By ECI
pieces.outlet: LiveLaw (Debby Jain), report of his oral submissions

pieces.title: Bihar SIR: 20 Lakh First-Time Voters Are Missing From Bihar's Draft Electoral Roll
pieces.outlet: The Wire (Pavan Korada; Yadav's calculation as told to The Wire)

pieces.title: Bihar SIR Key Takeaways: 'Missing Voters' Triple, Gender Skew Worse, 5 Lakh Voters With Gibberish Values
pieces.outlet: The Wire Staff, report of his presentation to the Supreme Court on 9 Oct 2025

pieces.title: BJP Using SIR To Cut Electorate In Opposition-Ruled States, Claims Yogendra Yadav
pieces.outlet: ETV Bharat (also carried by The Week as PTI copy)

claims.quote: a good electoral roll of Bihar should have 8 crore 18 lakh people, but it had 7.9 crores. So there was deficit of 29 lakhs to begin with
claims.rests: His oral submission in the Supreme Court, as LiveLaw reported it.
claims.site: The site uses the same kind of projection. It puts Bihar's adults at about 8.30 crore on 1 March 2026, against 7.90 crore on the roll before the revision and 7.24 crore on the draft. Across 19 states the rolls held 98.3 per cent of projected adults before the revision and 84.4 per cent on the drafts.
claims.stops: A projection counts residents. In a state that sends workers elsewhere it counts adults who may be registered where they came from, and the site says so beside the figure.

claims.quote: Total eligible adults: The government report projects Bihar's 18+ population in July 2025 at 8.18 crore ... New registered voters: The ECI's press release states that the new draft roll contains only 7.24 crore voters. The shortfall: 8.18 crore – 7.24 crore = 94 lakh.
claims.rests: His calculation as The Wire set it out. The arithmetic holds, and the ratio of electors to adults falls from 97 to 88 per cent.
claims.site: The site's figures move the same way. Bihar's draft held 7,24,05,756 names after 65,59,626 were left off in the first phase.
claims.stops: Part of the gap is young adults not yet enrolled and part is error in the projection, so the site does not call the whole of it disenfranchisement.

claims.quote: 25 lakh men and 31 lakh women have been deleted
claims.rests: His figures as LiveLaw reported them, with no source given. His reason, that more men migrate and die, is his own inference.
claims.site: The share matches the site's count closely, though the totals differ. The first-phase lists hold 36,39,976 women and 29,19,433 men, so women are 55.5 per cent of the names against 47.9 per cent of the roll. They are over-represented in all 38 districts and in 242 of 243 seats.
claims.stops: The lists do not say why. Moves on marriage account for about half a year's worth of the excess, and the district pattern runs against that explanation.

claims.quote: Never in the history of this country has any revision ever asked all people to submit a form or to submit a document. NEVER
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: Said in reply to a question about 2003, when he asked the Commission to produce the 2003 order, which he said was not public.
claims.site: The process page sets out what the 2025 order asked of electors, from the order itself.
claims.stops: The site has not compared the 2003 instructions.

claims.quote: We are witnessing perhaps the largest exercise of disenfranchisement, not in India, in the history of the world. Entire figure will cross 1 crore, if they are serious about what they are doing.
claims.rests: A forecast made in August 2025.
claims.site: The final roll did not bear the forecast out as stated. After the draft 3,66,742 more names were deleted and 21,53,343 added, and the final roll of 7,41,92,357 was 47,72,808 below the roll before the revision.
claims.stops: Disenfranchisement turns on who was eligible, and the lists record only the reason an officer wrote down.

claims.quote: From 27 lakh after the January 2025 special summary revision, the number of adults who are not registered as voters has gone up to 81 lakh in the SIR.
claims.rests: The Wire's account of his presentation to the Court. The article does not give his adult base, and 81 lakh plus the final roll implies about 8.23 crore.
claims.site: The same method on the site's projection of 8.30 crore gives about 88 lakh adults off the final roll.
claims.stops: As before, the projection counts residents.

claims.quote: From the outset, I have said SIR is targeted at Bengal. As Bihar elections were only a few months away, the EC used the state as the testing ground to implement SIR. Now the BJP wants to go the whole hog in Bengal
claims.outlet: PTI, as carried by ETV Bharat
claims.rests: A statement of purpose made at a public meeting in Kolkata, as PTI reported it.
claims.site: Nothing on the site measures purpose.
claims.stops: The site makes no claim about what anyone intended.

strongest: He measures the roll against the adult population, which catches young adults that a count of names left off cannot.
He pointed out early that more women than men were left off in Bihar, and the site's count of the lists bears it out in every district.
He raised problems in the final Bihar roll, entries with junk values and apparent duplicates, that can be checked against the roll.
further: Calling it the largest disenfranchisement in the history of the world, and saying it would cross 1 crore, were forecasts. Bihar's final roll fell by about 48 lakh.
He attributes a purpose to the BJP and the Commission from the choice of states alone.

people.name: Debraj Ray
people.role: Economist at New York University, writing as an individual in a research note on his own site.
people.intro: His note of 10 May 2026 asks whether the names West Bengal left off or deleted could account for the BJP's majority, and shows how the answer moves with each assumption.

pieces.title: SIR and the BJP's Bengal Majority

claims.quote: If we restrict ourselves to the adjudicated SIR deletions, and even if we make the incredibly heroic assumption that every deleted voter would have obediently turned out, and that every such voter would have voted for the runner-up ... that flips a maximum of 26 ACs away from the BJP. The resulting number, 207-26 =181, leaves the BJP comfortably above the 148-seat majority threshold
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: An upper bound under assumptions he states. It agrees with Newslaundry's count and with The Wire's, which reached 25.
claims.site: His state totals come from the same press note the site uses. They give 7,66,37,529 electors before the revision, 58,20,899 left off the draft, 60,06,675 held for adjudication and 27,16,393 found not eligible.
claims.stops: The Chief Electoral Officer has published no adjudication outcomes by constituency, so the site does not compute this bound.

claims.quote: Under any neutral calibration, the BJP retains majority by more than thirty seats. The deletions hypothesis only reverses this result at extreme calibrations that the data refuse to support
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: His widest bound, which counts the shifted and absent as well, flips 69 seats and leaves the BJP ten short of a majority. He argues it would need about 92 per cent turnout among those left off or deleted and about 95 per cent of them voting against the BJP.
claims.site: The site's Bihar estimate works the same way. In 187 of 243 seats the runner-up could not have won even with the vote of every elector left off or deleted, and the estimates have 4 to 6 seats changing hands in both directions.
claims.stops: No one knows how those electors would have voted. Where the site cannot assume it, it gives the share of votes the runner-up would have needed.

claims.quote: BJP MLAs were associated with more adjudicated deletions in their own seats, about 15 more per thousand voters ... It is consistent with the strategic-targeting story for the adjudication channel ... But the offsetting movement in non-adjudicated deletions along the same dimensions means that the overall contestable rate ... shows no partisan-targeting signal.
claims.kind: A pattern in the names left off or deleted
claims.rests: His strongest evidence of a partisan pattern. He calls it a correlation and states its limit in the same passage.
claims.site: The site measures the fall in the roll, a different count. Set against their own districts, seats the AITC won lost 0.23 more per 100 and seats the BJP won 0.03 more.
claims.stops: The site holds no adjudication figures by seat, so it cannot test his finding directly.

claims.quote: This is not an argument that the SIR did not matter. It clearly mattered in particular constituencies ... Why individuals had to be put through this ordeal in this particular election, with many plausibly denied their constitutional rights, is a question that should hold our attention.

strongest: He states every assumption and shows how the answer changes with it.
He separates the names deleted after adjudication, where a partisan pattern appears, from the names booth-level officers left off the draft, where none does.
further: He sets aside the 24.2 lakh entered as dead as exclusions that can be defended. In Bihar the site found deaths entered at about 3.4 years' worth, with women over-represented, so a death on the list is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.

people.name: Newslaundry
people.role: Independent news site funded by its subscribers. The analysis is by Samarth Grover.
people.intro: Its piece of 7 May 2026 runs four tests of rising strictness on the names West Bengal left off or deleted and reports how the answer shrinks.

pieces.title: 4 tests, 1 question: Did SIR shape Bengal outcome?

claims.quote: If we compare the 2026 winning margins to the net deletions in each constituency, we get 82 BJP-won constituencies where deletions exceeded the party's victory margin. Of these, 70 were seats that flipped from TMC to BJP.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: A count of seats where the names left off or deleted exceeded the margin, which the author calls the point where the data starts to raise questions.
claims.site: Measured by the fall in the roll from 2024, the site finds the fall larger than the margin in 139 of 294 seats, taking every party together.
claims.stops: A count larger than the margin measures size. It cannot show an effect.

claims.quote: An even stricter test, comparing UA deletions to the electoral swing from 2021, shows that in 14 seats, the deletions were higher than the overall change in margin. Of these 14, the BJP won only one – Pandabeswar – and the TMC won the rest in 2026.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: As published. The article adds that the TMC had won all 14 in 2021.
claims.site: The site has not run this test.
claims.stops: The site holds no count by seat of the names held for adjudication.

claims.quote: The assumption most commonly made – that the deleted voters were TMC's – deserves particular scepticism ... Both things can be true simultaneously: a revision can be administratively legitimate and electorally consequential

Whether that overlap reflects correction, disenfranchisement, or some combination of both may remain unresolved. That is a question of public interest that warrants a full and transparent answer, something which the Election Commission refuses to provide.
claims.rests: The article's closing paragraph.
claims.site: The site's figures stop at the same place.
claims.stops: The lists cannot tell a correct exclusion from a wrongful one, and the Commission has not published what would.

strongest: Four tests, each stated, with the answer shrinking from 82 seats to one, and an explicit refusal to claim a cause.
further: Very little. It calls the measure based on adjudication more targeted, which describes the measure and says nothing of intent.

people.name: Lokniti-CSDS
people.role: The survey programme of the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies, Delhi. The report quoted is The Wire's, by Pavan Korada.
people.intro: Its survey of August 2025, 3,054 interviews in five states and Delhi, asked who holds the documents the Commission's order listed.

pieces.title: 'SIR Risks Disenfranchising Millions of Legitimate Citizens Over Lack of Documents': Lokniti-CSDS Survey

claims.quote: A majority of respondents, 52%, do not have a birth certificate. Furthermore, 41% lack a domicile certificate and 42% do not possess a caste certificate.
claims.rests: Survey figures as The Wire reported them.
claims.site: The site has no survey of documents.
claims.stops: Lacking a document did not by itself keep anyone off the roll. In the later phases most electors were matched to the 2002 to 2005 rolls and asked for no document, and Aadhaar was later accepted on the Supreme Court's orders.

claims.quote: three-quarters of the citizens who have none of the required documents belong to the lower half of the economic order.
claims.rests: As The Wire reported it.
claims.site: The site does not measure household income. Its All India comparisons use each state's income per head.
claims.stops: The site cannot say who among those left off or deleted held which document.

claims.quote: the current requirements could pose a 'serious challenge for many of those who have a legitimate right to be part of the voters' list.'
claims.rests: A statement of risk, hedged in the report's own words.

strongest: It is the only independent survey of who holds the documents the order listed, and it hedges its own conclusion.
further: The Wire's headline, that the revision risks disenfranchising millions, is stronger than the survey's own wording.

people.name: Rahul Gandhi
people.role: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Congress MP, who has led his party's campaign against the revision since the Voter Adhikar Yatra in Bihar in 2025.
people.intro: The quotations come from four pieces. They are a post on his WhatsApp channel in August 2025 as PTI translated it, his press briefing in Delhi on 24 September 2026, his post on X of 5 October 2026, and the joint petition of INDIA bloc leaders to the Supreme Court as The Indian Express quoted it on 13 October 2026.

pieces.title: SIR is 'new weapon' of 'vote chori', will protect 'one person, one vote', says Rahul Gandhi
LoP Rahul Gandhi addresses Delhi press briefing amid ECI dissent row over SIR
Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 'illegally' during SIR, says Rahul Gandhi
Opposition to Supreme Court: Probe Election Commission decisions, audit of SIR voter deletions

claims.quote: SIR is a new weapon of vote theft. Coincidentally, these people standing with me in this picture are 'living' proof of this theft. ... All of them had cast their vote in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections - but by the time Bihar assembly elections came, their identity, their existence was erased from the democracy of India
claims.translation: PTI's translation from his Hindi post; The Hindu adds, in reported speech, that he said the collusion of the BJP and the Commission 'is punishing them for being Bahujan and poor'.
claims.rests: He rests the claim on six people from Bihar he met at Sasaram on 17 August 2025, who he says voted in 2024 and were missing from the draft roll. The quotation is PTI's English translation of his Hindi post, and the line about Bahujan and poor voters being punished is PTI's reported speech. The site has not checked the six cases.
claims.site: Bihar's phase 1 lists left 65,59,626 names off the draft. The lists record no caste, so the site guesses it from surnames in two ways, and the two point in different directions. In the first, Scheduled Castes were 20.0 per cent of the classified names left off against 19.65 per cent in the 2023 caste survey, and General names 34.4 per cent against 10.72. In the second, Scheduled Castes were 30.0 per cent and Muslim names 29.0 per cent. One group the lists do count was over-represented. Women were 55.5 per cent of those left off against 47.9 per cent of the roll.
claims.stops: Caste guessed from names is no identification, and the bounds on every group are wide. The site records nothing about income, so it cannot say whether those left off were poorer than other electors. It says nothing about what anyone intended.

claims.quote: let me tell you there is already more than enough information to make this a 100% certainty, not 99%, a 100% certainty that Indian elections, Lok Sabha elections, 2024 election, Vidhan Sabha elections, are all being rigged.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: He points to his earlier presentations on Maharashtra, Mahadevapura, Aland and Haryana and to information he says came from inside the Commission. The briefing sets out no figure behind the certainty.
claims.site: Bihar 2025 is the one election after a revision that the site has modelled. More names were left off the draft than the winning margin in 174 of 243 seats, and the net fall to the final roll exceeded the margin in 124. Estimating how the electors left off or deleted would have voted moves 4 to 6 seats, some each way, and the NDA keeps its majority on every estimate. A model of the swing that allows for each seat's 2020 lead gives a slope of +0.31, with a range from -0.27 to +0.89, which takes in no effect at all.
claims.stops: A count of names left off or deleted above the margin shows that they were large enough to decide a seat. It cannot show that they did. The 2024 Lok Sabha election came before the revision, and the site holds no evidence on changes to the roll before it.

claims.quote: Please understand what these two gentlemen are saying. They're saying that the vote does not exist in India anymore.
claims.rests: He refers to the Express investigation of 23 September 2026 into the two Election Commissioners' notes. The paper reports 14 objections, about Form 6, deletions and restorations, appeals in West Bengal and access to the roll software. It does not report either Commissioner saying the vote no longer exists.
claims.site: The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists each dated objection as the paper reported it. Among them are a note of 16 May 2026 that Form 6 cannot be changed without amending the 1960 Rules and a note of 13 August calling the change unauthorised and illegal.
claims.stops: The site has seen only the paper's account of the notes. His sentence is his own reading of them.

claims.quote: SIR came once we started saying there's a problem with voter deletion and addition it was a response to our questions and the idea was let us broad brush this and clean this thing out because we're going to get into trouble.
claims.rests: He gives his own account of the order of events and cites no document. The quotation is from the questions near the end of the briefing.
claims.site: The order of 24 June 2025 directed a Special Intensive Revision in the entire country, starting with Bihar. The joint petition he later signed alleges that no recorded decision of the full Commission authorised the nationwide revision. The Commission's press note 120 of 26 September 2026 says the order had its unanimous approval.
claims.stops: The site cannot say why the revision was ordered. It holds the order and the two competing accounts of how it was approved.

claims.quote: It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP. He and everyone else involved in this criminal assault on our democracy will be held accountable
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: His post of 5 October 2026 cites no document. It follows his post of 1 October, which cites the Commissioners' recorded objections as the Express reported them, and it came after the Supreme Court's remark of 5 October that it had not approved any modified Form 6.
claims.site: The Disputes page carries each step. The Express reported the declaration on the online Form 6 on 12 July 2026, and two Commissioners objected to it in writing. On 5 October the Chief Justice said in court that any modified Form 6 had not been approved by the Court. The Commission's press note 120 says the full Commission approved the declaration and kept it for the revision, and by 30 September it had been taken off the online form in states whose final roll was out.
claims.stops: No court has decided whether the change was lawful. The site cannot say who made it, and the Commission says all its decisions were unanimous. That it was done to help the BJP is his inference, and the records show nothing about purpose.

claims.quote: reportedly reflected a reduction of approximately 20.66 lakh names from the electorate of about 2.14 crore recorded in June 2026
claims.rests: These are the words of the joint writ petition filed on 12 October 2026 by INDIA bloc leaders, the bloc's petition, signed by him among others, as The Indian Express quotes it. The petition says reportedly, and rests on press reports of Punjab's figures.
claims.site: The figure matches the site's. Punjab's roll before the revision held 2,14,61,043 names and 20,66,635 were left off, 9.63 for every 100 electors. Of those, 5,74,568 were entered as dead, 13,56,846 as shifted, absent or other and 1,19,145 as duplicates. After the draft 7,97,263 names were added and 86,038 deleted, and the final roll of 12 October 2026 holds 2,01,00,727, a net fall of 13,60,343, or 6.34 for every 100.
claims.stops: Punjab's figures came through the press, given at the end of enumeration before the draft, and the published final-roll figures do not add up exactly. The rise after the draft counts new voters too, so the site does not call it names put back.

strongest: The Punjab figure in the bloc's petition matches the count the site holds.
On Form 6 his account of the record holds. Two Commissioners objected in writing, the Supreme Court said it had approved no modified form, and the declaration was later taken off the online form.
In Bihar more names were left off the draft than the winning margin in 174 of 243 seats, so exclusions large enough to decide a result were present.
further: He says it is certain that the 2024 and later elections were rigged. The site's one model of an election after a revision finds 4 to 6 seats moving, some each way, and no change of majority.
He reads the exclusions as falling on Bahujan and poor voters. The lists record neither caste nor income, and the site's two guesses at caste from names disagree.
He attributes a purpose to the Commission and to the Form 6 change, which the records cannot show.

people.name: Gyanesh Kumar, and the Election Commission of India
people.role: Chief Election Commissioner of India since February 2025. The panel also carries statements the Commission issued in its own name.
people.intro: His words come from press conferences in August and October 2025 and his National Voters' Day statement of January 2026, as The Indian Express, The Wire and PTI reported them. The Commission's statements come from its clarification of 23 September 2026 and its press note 120 of 26 September, as The Hindu and NDTV reproduced them and as the Commission published the press note.

pieces.title: Give affidavit in 7 days or apologise to nation: CEC to Rahul as his Bihar yatra hits the road
On Bihar Election Trail, Shah Brings Up 'Illegal Immigrants' on Rolls, But EC Provided No Figures
SIR rollout in remaining States soon: CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Dissent row: Election Commission says highlighting certain internal notes gives only one side of the picture
Election Commission "Fact-Checks" Rahul Gandhi's Form 6 Allegations

claims.quote: Halafnama dena hoga ya desh se maafi maangni hogi, koi teesra vikalp nahi hai… Agar saath din mein halafnama nahi mila to iska arth, ki yeh saare aarop niradhar hai.
claims.translation: Either give an affidavit or apologise to the nation, there is no third option. If an affidavit is not received within seven days, it would mean that these allegations are baseless. (The Indian Express's translation.)
claims.rests: The Express gives his Hindi words in Roman script with its own translation. The test he sets is whether an accuser signs an affidavit within seven days. At the same conference he did not say how many electors on the draft had submitted documents or how many foreign nationals had been found.
claims.site: Bihar's draft left off 65,59,626 names for four reasons as officers entered them. Officers entered 22,32,586 as dead, 26,55,900 as shifted, 9,70,081 as absent and 7,01,059 as already enrolled.
claims.stops: A reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. Whether an affidavit is filed says nothing about whether the roll is right, and the site cannot say whether any allegation about it is true.

claims.quote: The names deleted from the electoral rolls include those who have died, those who are not Indian citizens, those who are registered in multiple places and those who have shifted permanently. The responsibility to create the electoral roll is of the ERO [electoral registration officer]. So every ERO and every district magistrate has this data
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: He spoke at a press conference in Patna on 5 October 2025, five days after Bihar's final roll. The words are The Wire's English, and the language he spoke in was not found.
claims.site: None of the reasons in Bihar's published records is citizenship. The phase 1 lists give four reasons, dead, shifted, absent and already enrolled, for 65,59,626 names. After the draft the Commission's return lists 3,66,742 deleted, 62,441 as expired, 2,12,999 as shifted, 81,334 as repeated and 9,968 with no reason stated. In May 2026 the Supreme Court directed the Commission to refer any cases it had deleted as non-citizens to the authority under the Citizenship Act. Such cases may exist, and no count of them has been published.
claims.stops: The site says nothing about whether any person is a citizen. A recorded reason is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.

claims.quote: Many times, if any individual who is not an Indian citizen and who has got some papers made, you would have noticed, that in the enumeration phase we will match whether in 2002, 2003 or 2004, either you or your senior relatives were on the electoral rolls or not. If there is a match, then the matter ends there. Those who do not match, they will be issued a notice, after this they will have to show their papers and say where they were in 2003. Doing this is very necessary
claims.translation: The Wire's English; the original was likely Hindi and was not seen.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: He spoke when the Commission announced the second phase on 27 October 2025. The words are The Wire's English. He describes the procedure the order sets out.
claims.site: The order of 27 October 2025 asked for no documents at enumeration and sent notices after the draft to electors who could not be linked to the last intensive revision. Across the 21 states that have published a total, 13,06,52,476 electors kept on the drafts were sent a notice, 21.1 for every 100.
claims.stops: A notice records that an elector could not be linked to the old roll or that the entry showed a discrepancy. It is no finding about citizenship, and the site never treats it as one.

claims.quote: The most compelling testament to the success of the SIR in Bihar was that not a single appeal was filed against the final electoral roll, establishing its sanctity and credibility
claims.rests: PTI quotes his statement of National Voters' Day, 24 January 2026, and NDTV quotes him saying the same on 27 October 2025. The count of appeals is the Commission's own and has not been published. Amit Shah said on 29 October 2025 that three appeals had been made against the deletions. Neither count is published, and the two may count different things.
claims.site: From the Commission's return, 65,59,409 names were left off Bihar's draft, 21,53,343 were added after it and 3,66,742 deleted, and the final roll of 7,41,92,357 is 47,72,808 smaller than the roll before. The Supreme Court in May 2026 opened judicial review to people it called erroneously deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate. In West Bengal, where adjudication outcomes were reported, 22,21,118 appeals were filed by people excluded, as reported.
claims.stops: The site has no count of appeals in Bihar, so it cannot confirm or refute zero. An appeal needs someone who knows their name was left off or deleted and is able to file one, so a lack of appeals cannot show that the exclusions and deletions were right.

claims.quote: All decisions of the Election Commission of India, including SIR [the ongoing special intensive revision of electoral rolls], have been unanimous and with the approval of both the Election Commissioners and the Chief Election Commissioner
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: This is the Commission's clarification of 23 September 2026, as The Hindu printed it. The same day a written statement said, in The Hindu's reported speech, that differing views are a normal part of deliberation in any institution. Press note 120 of 26 September repeats that the order and the schedules had unanimous approval.
claims.site: The Commission does not dispute that the notes exist. The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists them as the Express reported them. Among them are a note of 16 May 2026 that Form 6 cannot be changed without amending the Rules, a second Commissioner's agreement on 19 May, and a note of 13 August calling the change unauthorised and illegal and directing its removal. By 30 September the declaration had been taken off the online form in states whose final roll was out.
claims.stops: The notes are press reports, and the site has not seen them. The site cannot say which decisions the statement of unanimity covers.

claims.quote: The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: The sentence is from the Commission's press note 120 of 26 September 2026, which the Commission repeated on X in reply to Rahul Gandhi. It refers to the Supreme Court's judgment of 27 May 2026 on the Bihar revision.
claims.site: The judgment upheld the Bihar order of 24 June 2025, which asked for a declaration in Annexure D with Form 6. In the site's reading it makes no separate finding on the declaration. The declaration two Commissioners objected to in 2026 was added later to the online Form 6. On 5 October 2026 the Chief Justice said in court that any modified Form 6 had not been approved by the Court.
claims.stops: It reports the hearing of 5 October as LiveLaw reported it.

strongest: His account of the second phase, matching electors to the old rolls and sending notices to those who could not be linked, describes the procedure as the order sets it out.
The reasons he gives for exclusion include the ones the records carry, death, duplicate entries and shifting.
On the internal notes the Commission did not deny that they exist, and it said differing views are part of deliberation.
further: He names non-citizens among the names left off or deleted in Bihar, which no published count shows.
He treats the absence of appeals as proof of the roll's credibility. An appeal needs a person who knows they were left off or deleted and is able to file one.

The Commission says the Supreme Court upheld the Form 6 declaration. That goes further than the judgment as the site reads it, and the Chief Justice said on 5 October that the Court had approved no modified form.

people.name: Amit Shah
people.role: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation and a BJP leader, who spoke for the government in the Lok Sabha debate on electoral reforms on 10 December 2025.
people.intro: The quotations come from his post on X of 29 October 2025, the Press Information Bureau's English account of his Lok Sabha speech of 10 December 2025, and The Indian Express's report of a rally at Cooch Behar on 15 April 2026. The speech and the rally were in Hindi, so those quotations are English renderings by PIB and the Express.

pieces.title: Post on X, 29 Oct 2025
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah participates in discussion on electoral reforms in Lok Sabha
pieces.outlet: Press Information Bureau (Ministry of Home Affairs)

pieces.title: EC removed infiltrators from roll, we'll remove them from Bengal's soil: Amit Shah

claims.quote: बिहार में SIR के बाद केवल तीन ही अपील आए, जिसका मतलब है कि घुसपैठियों के नाम कटे हैं।
claims.translation: After the SIR in Bihar only three appeals came in, which means it is the names of infiltrators that were cut.
claims.rests: The post is his own, in Hindi, and the translation is the site's. He does not say where the count of three appeals comes from. The Chief Election Commissioner said no appeal was filed against the final roll, while Shah spoke of appeals against the deletions. Neither count is published, and they may count different things.
claims.site: Officers entered Bihar's 65,59,626 names left off the draft under four reasons. Of these, 22,32,586 were entered as dead, 26,55,900 as shifted, 9,70,081 as absent and 7,01,059 as already enrolled. Set against death records, the dead come to about 3.4 years of adult deaths at the right ages, though 52.0 per cent of them are women against 43.4 per cent of deaths. After the draft 3,66,742 more were deleted as expired, shifted, repeated or with no reason stated.
claims.stops: The site says nothing about whether anyone is a citizen. A count of appeals cannot show who was left off or deleted, and none of the reasons in Bihar's lists is citizenship. A reason is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.

claims.quote: He explained that Special Intensive Revision (SIR) involves removing names due to death or duplicate entries (people registered in two places), adding names when a person turns 18, and selectively deleting those who are foreign citizens.
claims.translation: PIB's reported speech in English, not his words verbatim.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: This is PIB's English reported speech of his Hindi speech, and his own words were not found. PIB's summary at the top of the same release renders the last part as selectively deleting infiltrators.
claims.site: Across the 31 states and union territories with a draft, 13,39,03,307 names were left off. Of these 2,79,69,558, or 20.9 per cent, were entered as dead, 9,56,35,923, or 71.5 per cent, as shifted, absent or other, and 1,01,48,459, or 7.6 per cent, as duplicates.
claims.stops: Deaths and duplicates are recorded reasons in every state, as he says. No published figure counts the names left off or deleted by citizenship, and the site does not estimate one. The largest group in the records is neither dead nor duplicate.

claims.quote: He said that even if the opposition boycotts the House 200 times, we will not allow even a single illegal infiltrator to vote in the country. The Home Minister said that the government’s policy is to Detect, Delete, and Deport, and we will carry out this work through constitutional processes.
claims.translation: PIB's reported speech in English.
claims.rests: This is PIB's English reported speech of his Hindi speech, and his own words were not found. PIB's body calls it the government's policy and its highlight calls it the party's. It is a statement of policy and carries no count.
claims.site: The Supreme Court held in May 2026 that deciding citizenship belongs to the authority under the Citizenship Act and that declining to enrol someone does not declare that person not to be a citizen. The Commission's instructions of 14 May 2026 tell registration officers to refer suspected foreign nationals to that authority.
claims.stops: The site says nothing about whether anyone is a citizen, and the revision's records carry no finding on it.

claims.quote: Union Home Minister said that the beginning of our democratic history was in 1952, and the first Special Intensive Revision took place in 1952. ... He said that after 2004, the next Special Intensive Revision is taking place only in 2025, and no political party has ever opposed this process till date
claims.translation: PIB's reported speech in English.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: This is PIB's English reported speech of his Hindi speech. He lists intensive revisions in 1952, 1957, 1961, 1965, 1966, 1983-84, 1987-89, 1992-95 and 2002-04.
claims.site: The revisions of 2002 to 2004 are the base most states are mapped to now, which agrees with his last date. Bihar and Uttar Pradesh map to 2003, and West Bengal and Kerala to 2002. By the day he spoke, a Trinamool Congress MP had petitioned the Supreme Court in July 2025, the DMK, CPI(M), Congress and Trinamool had filed pleas heard in November, the Samajwadi Party had filed one on 9 December, and the Jharkhand and Kerala Assemblies had passed resolutions against the revision.
claims.stops: The site has not researched revisions before 2002 and cannot check his list. On the current revision, the record of petitions and resolutions does not bear out the statement that no party has opposed it.

claims.quote: Till now, the EC has only removed the names of the infiltrators from the electoral rolls, but we will remove them from the soil of Bengal.
claims.translation: The Indian Express's English. The Telegraph renders the same sentence as 'While the Election Commission (EC) has only removed infiltrators from the electoral rolls of West Bengal, the larger task would be to drive them out of the country's borders.'
claims.rests: The Indian Express gives his words in English, and The Telegraph renders the same Hindi sentence differently. The Express says he was referring to over 89 lakh names, and The Telegraph to nearly 91 lakh.
claims.site: West Bengal's draft left off 58,20,899 names. Officers entered 24,16,852 as dead and 1,38,328 as duplicates. The other 32,65,719 were shifted, absent or other, and the largest part of them, 19,88,076, as shifted, so death is the largest single reason. A further 60,06,675 were held for adjudication. As reported, 32,68,119 were found eligible and 27,16,393 not eligible, with no reason published, and 22,21,118 appeals were filed by people excluded.
claims.stops: No published figure counts the names left off or deleted by citizenship. Being found not eligible in adjudication is no finding that a person is a foreigner, and the site says nothing about whether anyone is a citizen.

strongest: He says the revision takes the dead and those registered twice off the roll, and the records of every state carry both reasons.
His date for the last intensive revision, 2002 to 2004, agrees with the rolls most states are mapped to now.
further: He reads Bihar's few appeals as showing that infiltrators were taken off the roll. The reasons officers recorded in Bihar are death, shifting, absence and duplicate entry, and no published figure counts anyone left off or deleted as a foreigner.
He describes the names West Bengal left off or deleted as infiltrators, though the largest reason entered there is death and no reason has been published for those found not eligible.
He says no party has ever opposed the process, though parties had gone to the Supreme Court and two Assemblies had passed resolutions before he spoke.

people.name: Yogi Adityanath
people.role: Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, of the BJP.
people.intro: Three of the quotations are from his speech to BJP workers in Lucknow on 14 December 2025, in his own words from the video of the speech. The fourth is from his own post on X of 5 October 2026. The translations are the site's.

pieces.title: CM Yogi Speech : 'यूपी में चार करोड़ मतदाता मिसिंग', SIR की प्रक्रिया पर CM Yogi ने जताई चिंता
pieces.title_en: CM Yogi's speech: 'Four crore voters missing in UP', CM Yogi raises concern about the SIR process

pieces.title: Post on X

claims.quote: 18 वर्ष से ऊपर का मतदाता मतदाता सूची में नाम होना चाहिए। तो यह संख्या होनी चाहिए 16 करोड़। और मतदाता सूची में एसआईआर के बाद जो मतदाता सूची में नाम आए हैं वो कितने आए हैं? 12 करोड़। यह 4 करोड़ का जो गैप है 2025 की जो मतदाता सूची थी जनवरी 2025 की उसमें कुल नाम थे 15 करोड़ 44 लाख
claims.translation: Every voter over 18 should be on the roll, so this number should be 16 crore. And how many names have come onto the roll after the SIR? 12 crore. This gap of 4 crore. The roll of January 2025 had 15 crore 44 lakh names.
claims.rests: His own arithmetic in the speech. He took a population of about 25 crore and a share of 64 to 65 per cent adults to reach 16 crore who should be on the roll, and set it against the 12 crore enumeration forms collected by mid-December 2025, three weeks before the draft. The 15 crore 44 lakh is the roll of January 2025.
claims.site: His 15 crore 44 lakh matches the roll before the revision, 15,44,30,092. The draft of 6 January 2026 held 12,55,56,025, close to his 12 crore. The draft was 2,88,74,067 names below the old roll, which is 2.89 crore. Set against the site's projection of 16,16,85,000 people aged 18 and over on 1 March 2026, the draft was 3.61 crore short. So his four crore sets the roll against a population projection. The roll before held 95.51 electors per 100 projected adults and the draft 77.65. The final roll of 10 April 2026 held 13,39,84,792 names, 82.87 per 100 projected adults.
claims.stops: The projection counts residents, and they are not all on the roll anywhere. It takes in people registered in another state and adults who never enrolled. So a shortfall against it is no count of names left off, and 16 crore is an upper bound on who could be on Uttar Pradesh's roll.

claims.quote: यह जो 4 करोड़ का गैप है, यह मिसिंग है। यह आपका विरोधी नहीं है। इसमें से 85 से 90% आपका मतदाता है।
claims.translation: This gap of 4 crore is missing. It is not your opponent. 85 to 90 per cent of it is your voter.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: No source is given. He says it in the video of the speech. The Hindustan Times prints the line in English as 'Eighty-five to 90 per cent of these missing voters are ours'. The Indian Express has 90 per cent, which does not match the video.
claims.site: No published record says how any elector left off votes. The site can show where the exclusions fell. They were heaviest in the towns and cities, 28.12 per 100 on the urban roll against 15.25 on the rural roll, by the Chief Electoral Officer's figures as the Hindustan Times printed them. Lucknow lost the most, 30.04 per 100. When each district's rate is spread over its constituencies, seats the NDA won in 2022 lost about 19.14 per 100 and seats the SP alliance won about 17.69.
claims.stops: That small difference is about places. It says nothing about the people left off, and the site cannot say whom any of them would have voted for.

claims.quote: देखिए मैं अभी गया था एक जनपद में। वहां की मतदाता सूची में जो एसआईआर के फॉर्म भरे हैं बहुत सारी विरोधियों ने उसमें कुछ बांग्लादेशियों के भी नाम है। आप मुझे बताइए एक जगह तो यह भी मैंने देखा एक सज्जन का नाम था उसकी उम्र 20 साल। उसके पिता की उम्र 30 साल और उसके ग्रैंडफादर की उम्र 40 साल।
claims.translation: Look, I just went to a district. In the SIR forms filled in the roll there, many by opponents, there are names of some Bangladeshis too. Tell me, in one place I even saw a gentleman's name, his age 20, his father's age 30 and his grandfather's age 40.
claims.rests: His own account, in the video of the speech, of a visit to a district he does not name. He gives no figure.
claims.site: No published figure counts the names left off or deleted by citizenship. The reasons officers wrote down at the draft are death, untraceable or absent, permanently shifted, enrolled more than once and others. Of the 8,15,996 names that came off after the draft, the press reported 2,069 recorded as under age or not citizens. On the ages he describes, electors whose link to the old roll showed a mismatch were sent a logical discrepancy notice, and the press reported 2.22 crore such notices in Uttar Pradesh. The site has found no Commission document that defines the category.
claims.stops: A reason is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. The site says nothing about whether any person or group is a citizen, and it cannot test what he saw on his visit.

claims.quote: सभी जागरूक मतदाता ध्यान रखें कि मतदाता सूची में अवैध रूप से दर्ज अपात्र नामों की पहचान कर उन्हें नियमानुसार हटाना भारत की सुरक्षा, एकता और अखंडता के लिए अनिवार्य है।
claims.translation: Every aware voter should keep in mind that identifying ineligible names illegally entered in the voter list and removing them according to the rules is essential for India's security, unity and integrity.
claims.rests: His own post on X of 5 October 2026, in Hindi. The same post says the dead, the permanently shifted and duplicate entries must be verified according to the rules. PTI's English rendering, carried by ThePrint, leaves out its opening words to every aware voter.
claims.site: The reasons officers wrote down at the draft are almost all about people who died, moved or are listed twice, and none is named as illegal entry. Of the names left off, 16.01 per cent were entered as dead, 27.54 as untraceable or absent, 44.95 as shifted, 8.82 as enrolled more than once and 2.68 as others. The one recorded reason near his word illegally, under age or not a citizen, covered 2,069 of the 8,15,996 names deleted after the draft, as reported. The largest group deleted after the draft, 3,50,026, were people sent a notice who did not answer.
claims.stops: A reason is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. The figures after the draft are press reports. The site says nothing about whether anyone on or off the roll is a citizen.

strongest: His figure for the roll before the revision, 15 crore 44 lakh, is right, and his 12 crore is close to the draft of 12,55,56,025.
The roll did fall well short of the adult population. The draft held 77.65 electors per 100 projected adults, against 95.51 before the revision.
His post names the dead, the shifted and duplicate entries as what must be checked, and those are the reasons officers recorded for almost every name left off.
further: His gap of four crore sets the roll against a population projection, and the projection counts residents who are not all on the roll anywhere. Against the old roll the draft was 2.89 crore smaller.
Saying 85 to 90 per cent of those missing are his party's voters goes beyond any record, since nothing published says how an elector left off or deleted votes.
Tying the exclusions to names entered illegally goes further than the officers' own records, which give under age or not a citizen as the reason for 2,069 names after the draft, as reported.

people.name: Mamata Banerjee
people.role: Chairperson of the All India Trinamool Congress, and Chief Minister of West Bengal when the revision began there.
people.intro: The quotations come from four reports between November 2025 and September 2026. They are a Bengali report of her speech at the end of a march in Kolkata, her letter to the Chief Election Commissioner as The New Indian Express printed it, and two speeches as reported in English. The translation from Bengali is the site's.

pieces.title: Mamata Banerjee on SIR: 'বিহারে কতজন রোহিঙ্গা চিহ্নিত, অসমে কেন এসআইআর নয়?' প্রশ্ন মমতার
pieces.title_en: How many Rohingyas were identified in Bihar, why no SIR in Assam? Mamata asks
pieces.outlet: News18 Bangla, report of her speech at the end of the anti-SIR march in Kolkata

pieces.title: Three to four people dying in West Bengal every day due to SIR anxiety: Mamata
pieces.outlet: The Hindu, carrying PTI's report of her speech at Red Road, Kolkata

pieces.title: 'SIR was conducted to help BJP capture Bengal': Mamata mounts attack on EC
pieces.outlet: The Indian Express (Express News Service, Kolkata)

pieces.title: Bengal CM Mamata blames SIR pressure for BLO deaths; urges EC to halt drive in Bengal

claims.quote: আমার প্রথম প্রশ্ন, অসমে কেন করলেন না SIR? আসলে অসমে ভুয়ো ভোটে জেতেন। এসআইআর করলে অসমে হেরে যেতেন। আমার দ্বিতীয় প্রশ্ন, উত্তর পূর্ব ভারতের রাজ্যগুলোতে কেন এসআইআর করলেন না? ত্রিপুরা দিয়েও তো বাংলাদেশিরা ঢোকে।
claims.translation: My first question: why did you not do the SIR in Assam? In fact you win Assam on fake votes. If you did the SIR you would lose Assam. My second question: why did you not do the SIR in the states of the North-East? Bangladeshis come in through Tripura too.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: The Commission's order of 27 October 2025, which named twelve states and union territories for the second phase and left out Assam and the North-East. Her words are in Bengali, from News18 Bangla's report, and the translation is the site's.
claims.site: The point about the process held when she said it. Assam was given a Special Revision by the Commission's order of 17 November 2025, with no enumeration forms and no link to an earlier roll, and it has never had an SIR. In that revision 10,56,291 names were flagged as dead, shifted or multiple. The North-East came later. The order of 14 May 2026 put Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Tripura in the third phase, and Tripura's enumeration ran from 15 September to 14 October 2026, with its draft due on 21 October.
claims.stops: The site's records cannot test her claims about fake votes in Assam or about who crosses into India through Tripura. Nothing the site holds counts entries by nationality, and it says nothing about whether any person or group is a citizen.

claims.quote: Several others have lost their lives since this process began. A revision that previously required three years is now being forcibly compressed into three months, subjecting BLOs and officials to inhuman working conditions and forcing common people under the shadow of fear and uncertainty.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: Her letter of 20 November 2025, as The New Indian Express printed it. She posted the letter as an image, and The Telegraph's version paraphrases it.
claims.site: Three months is about right for the schedule as first ordered. Enumeration in West Bengal ran from 4 November to 4 December 2025, later extended to 11 December. The draft came on 16 December, and the final roll, first due on 7 February and then on 14 February, was published on 28 February 2026. That is about four months from the first house visit to the final roll, and the 60,06,675 names put under adjudication were decided after it. The site's list of deaths reported during the revision has two items from West Bengal, both reported after this letter.
claims.stops: The site holds no record of how long earlier intensive revisions took, so it does not check her three years. It does not count deaths.

claims.quote: More than 110 people have already died; every day, three to four people are dying out of SIR anxiety
claims.rests: No list is given in the report, which is PTI's account of her speech at Red Road in Kolkata, carried by The Hindu. The English is the agency's, for words she may have spoken in Bengali. Her figure rose over the weeks. On 2 December 2025, announcing Rs 2 lakh for each family, she gave 39 deaths.
claims.site: No official count of deaths linked to the revision has been published. The site's list of deaths reported during the revision has eight items across India. Two are about West Bengal electors called to hearings. One is a 75-year-old man who fell ill in a hearing queue in Birbhum, in a report that also mentions an elderly man who died at a hearing in Howrah. The other is an 82-year-old man in Purulia whose son filed an FIR after he died, allegedly by suicide, hours before a hearing. Each is a press report of what a family alleged.
claims.stops: The site cannot say how many people died, or why, so neither 110 nor three to four a day can be checked here.

claims.quote: SIR was conducted in Bengal to capture the state. Ninety-three lakh names were either deleted or put under adjudication.
claims.rests: No source is given in the report. She spoke at a rally in Serampore in Hooghly, likely in Bengali, and the English is The Indian Express's.
claims.site: The 93 lakh is near the site's figures, depending on what is added. The draft left off 58,20,899 names, and 5,46,053 more came off on Form 7 after it. Of the 60,06,675 put under adjudication, 27,16,393 were found not eligible and 32,68,119 eligible, as reported. The draft, Form 7 and those found not eligible add to 90,83,345, about 91 lakh. Below the state the site has the fall in the roll, 77,58,998 from the 2024 roll to the roll the 2026 election was held on. That fall was larger than the winning margin in 139 of 294 seats, and larger than the margin at the seat's turnout in 132.
claims.stops: The adjudication outcomes are state totals as reported. Below the state the site has only the fall in the roll, never the names left off. Larger than the margin means those names could have decided a seat, never that they did, and nothing in the records shows why the revision was run.

strongest: Her question about Assam rested on a real difference in process. Assam had a Special Revision with no enumeration forms, and the North-East was added to the SIR only in May 2026.
Her 93 lakh is close to the site's own sum of names left off at the draft, deleted on Form 7 and found not eligible after adjudication, 90,83,345, as reported.
Three months is about right for the enumeration, the draft and the claims as first ordered.
further: Saying the SIR was run to capture the state is a claim about purpose, and nothing in the records shows why it was run.
Her count of more than 110 deaths, and three to four a day, rests on no published list. The site's own list of reported deaths has two items from West Bengal.
Saying the BJP wins Assam on fake votes is something no record the site holds can test.
